title_en: Li Haifeng et al. v. Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, Anhui Television Station, et al. — dispute over infringement of right to reputation and right to portrait
ruling_gist_en: When providing relevant materials of solved cases to news media for news reporting, public security authorities shall exercise a duty of prudent care to protect the lawful rights and interests of others. Failure to fulfill this duty, resulting in infringement of others' right to reputation, shall bear corresponding civil liability. The legality of the public security authority's investigation, the legitimacy of cooperating with news media for legal publicity, and the negligence of the news media itself in reporting do not constitute statutory grounds for exempting the public security authority from the aforementioned civil liability.

full_text_en:
Li Haifeng et al. v. Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, Anhui Television Station, et al. — dispute over infringement of reputation and portraiture rights

Ruling Summary

When a public security authority provides materials related to the detection of criminal cases to news media for news reporting, it shall exercise a duty of prudent care to protect the lawful rights and interests of others. Failure to fulfill this duty resulting in infringement of the reputation rights of others shall give rise to corresponding civil liability. The legality of the public security authority's investigative acts, the legitimacy of cooperating with news media for legal publicity, and the negligence of the news media itself in news reporting shall not constitute statutory grounds for exempting the public security authority from the aforesaid civil liability.

Plaintiffs:
1. Li Haifeng, male, 15 years old, student, residing in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Guardian: Li Qingguo (father of Li Haifeng), self-employed, address same as Li Haifeng.
2. Gao Ping, male, 14 years old, student, residing in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Guardian: Zhang Rong (mother of Gao Ping), farmer, address same as Gao Ping.
3. Liu Lei, male, 15 years old, student, residing in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Guardian: Zhang Yanling (mother of Liu Lei), laid-off worker of Huoqiu County Supply and Marketing Cooperative, address same as Liu Lei.
4. Sun Jun, male, 17 years old, student, residing in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Guardian: Sun Lisheng (father of Sun Jun), self-employed, address same as Sun Jun.
5. Chen Guanggui, male, 15 years old, student, residing in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Guardian: Chen Shuren (father of Chen Guanggui), self-employed, address same as Chen Guanggui.
6. Zhang Libao, male, 16 years old, student, residing in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Guardian: Zhang Hongwei (father of Zhang Libao), self-employed, address same as Zhang Libao.

Defendants:
1. Anhui Television Station, domiciled at: Tongcheng South Road, Hefei City.
   Legal Representative: Tang Daxiang, Director of the Station.
2. Yeji Reform and Development Experimental Zone Branch of Lu'an Public Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau), domiciled at: Yeji Reform and Development Experimental Zone, Lu'an City, Anhui Province.
   Person in Charge: Huang Jiayu, Director of the Sub-bureau.
3. Yeji Experimental School of Yeji Reform and Development Experimental Zone (hereinafter referred to as Yeji Experimental School), domiciled at: Yeji Experimental Zone, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province.
   Legal Representative: Zheng Changfu, Principal of the School.

The plaintiffs, Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, and Zhang Libao, filed an action with the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City, Anhui Province, alleging infringement of their reputation and portraiture rights against the defendants, Anhui Television Station, Yeji Reform and Development Experimental Zone Branch of Lu'an Public Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau), and Yeji Experimental School of Yeji Reform and Development Experimental Zone (hereinafter referred to as Yeji Experimental School).

Plaintiffs' Allegations: The six plaintiffs were all junior high school students of the defendant Yeji Experimental School. On April 13, 2005, the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau contacted Yeji Experimental School, and the class teacher notified the six plaintiffs to go to the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau to assist in the investigation of a rape (attempted) case. At the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, the six plaintiffs, as arranged by the police officers, held numbered placards and lined up with the criminal suspect to be identified by the victim, and were video-recorded. The six plaintiffs were not informed in advance of the true nature and purpose of the recording and later requested that it not be made public; the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau agreed but subsequently provided the video materials to the news media. On April 16, 2005, the "First Time" column of the defendant Anhui Television Station publicly reported the news, broadcast the video materials provided by the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, and did not explain the true circumstances of the six plaintiffs' assistance in the police investigation, nor did it make any technical processing of the relevant images. As members of the public were unaware of the truth, they condemned the six plaintiffs for committing heinous crimes while still minors, which negatively impacted the plaintiffs' lives and studies and caused tremendous mental stress to their families. The acts of the three defendants infringed upon the portraiture and reputation rights of the six plaintiffs. They requested that the court order the three defendants to publicly apologize, restore reputation, and eliminate the adverse effects; and pay each of the six plaintiffs RMB 100,000 in mental distress damages, totaling RMB 600,000.

To support their claims, the six plaintiffs, including Li Haifeng, submitted testimonial materials from Zhang Aiguo, a teacher of the defendant Yeji Experimental School, and a duplicate audio-visual recording of the news report in question broadcast on the "First Time" column of Anhui Television Station, to prove the truth of the alleged facts.

Defendant Anhui Television Station's Defense: The statements of Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs are inconsistent with the facts. Our station reported objectively occurring events based on the principle of respecting the truth, and there was no content insulting or defaming the six plaintiffs. When broadcasting the news, although no image processing was done on the images of the six plaintiffs, the images of the actual criminal suspect, Zhu Moumou, were processed, and the image of Zhu Moumou pressing his fingerprint was highlighted. Therefore, our station's actions did not infringe upon the reputation or portraiture rights of the six plaintiffs, nor did they cause any adverse effects. Hence, the plaintiffs' claims against our station should be dismissed.

The defendant Anhui Television Station did not provide evidence.

Defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau's Defense: The entire identification procedure on the evening of April 13, 2005, conducted by our bureau, complied with legal procedures and was not improper. The defendant Anhui Television Station's broadcast of the news in question was for the public interest of society and did not constitute infringement. Our bureau passively provided the video materials in question during an interview, and Anhui Television Station broadcast the video without obtaining our prior consent. Our bureau did not infringe upon the reputation or portraiture rights of Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs. The plaintiffs' request for mental distress damages has no legal basis. Therefore, the plaintiffs' claims against our bureau should be dismissed.

The defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau submitted the case registration form, decision to initiate investigation, detention warrant, detention notice, request for approval of arrest, approval decision for arrest, arrest warrant, arrest notice, interrogation record, identification record, and the (2005) Huo Xing Chu Zi No. 133 Criminal Judgment of Huoqiu County People's Court, to prove that the bureau's actions in solving the case were lawful, and not a fabrication of false news as alleged by the six plaintiffs. It also submitted a recommendation letter sent to the defendant Yeji Experimental School, to prove that on July 2, 2005, the bureau recommended that Yeji Experimental School commend the six plaintiffs.

Defendant Yeji Experimental School's Defense: Our school, at the request of the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, had the class teacher lead Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs to the bureau to assist in the mixed identification of the criminal suspect. The defendant Anhui Television Station broadcast the identification video without prior notice to our school, let alone obtaining our consent. The six plaintiffs' request that our school bear joint liability for compensation with the other two defendants has no factual or legal basis. Therefore, the claims against our school should be dismissed.

The defendant Yeji Experimental School applied for the testimony of Zhang Aiguo, a teacher of the school, to appear in court. Zhang Aiguo testified: On April 13, 2005, the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau notified the school that a criminal case required student participation in a mixed identification procedure. Under the assignment of school leadership, around 11:00 p.m. that evening, I led Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs to the conference room of the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau. Subsequently, the police officers arranged for the six plaintiffs to participate in the identification activity, which lasted about ten minutes. On April 16, the defendant Anhui Television Station broadcast the news, without prior notice to the school.

During cross-examination, the three defendants all denied the evidentiary purpose of the evidence provided by the six plaintiffs. The six plaintiffs argued that the evidence provided by the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau was irrelevant to this case. The defendant Anhui Television Station and the defendant Yeji Experimental School had no objection to the evidence submitted by the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau. After examination, the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City confirmed the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the video material of the news in question provided by the six plaintiffs, and confirmed the validity of the testimony of witness Zhang Aiguo. The evidence submitted by the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau regarding the procedures for solving the relevant criminal case could only prove the legality of its investigative methods; it had insufficient relevance to the facts to be proved in this case, and therefore was not admitted.

Facts Found by the Court:

The Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City found through trial:

On March 20, 2005, a rape (attempted) case occurred in Yeji Town, Huoqiu County, Anhui Province. After the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau filed the case, it arrested the criminal suspect, Zhu Moumou, on the afternoon of April 13 of the same year. That evening, the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau intended to arrange a mixed identification of the criminal suspect by the victim and requested assistance from the defendant Yeji Experimental School, stating that several junior high school boys of similar age to the criminal suspect Zhu Moumou were needed to participate in the identification. Around 9:00 p.m. that evening, when evening self-study ended, the Dean of Studies of Yeji Experimental School explained the matter to Zhang Aiguo, the class teacher of Class 8, Grade 2 of the junior high school, and Zhang Aiguo then led the plaintiffs Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Chen Guanggui, Zhang Libao, and Sun Jun to the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau. The police officers of the sub-bureau explained the relevant content of the mixed identification to Zhang Aiguo and the six plaintiffs. After Zhang Aiguo signed the interview record, the six plaintiffs, as instructed by the police officers, held numbered placards and lined up with the criminal suspect Zhu Moumou to be identified; this process was video-recorded and photographed by the police officers. The next day, a reporter from the defendant Anhui Television Station went to the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau to gather news. The Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau provided the relevant video materials of the identification process to the Anhui Television Station reporter without any instructions. On April 16, 2005, in the news broadcast by the "First Time" column of Anhui Television Station, images of Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs holding numbered placards and participating in the identification appeared, with their faces not technically obscured, lasting approximately two seconds. Anhui Television Station did not notify the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau or Yeji Experimental School before broadcasting this news. After Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs successively watched the news, they immediately raised objections to the school and the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, to no avail. Subsequently, they were called names such as "suspects" and "No. X rapist" by classmates and others. On July 2, 2005, the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau sent a recommendation letter to Yeji Experimental School, recommending that the school commend the six plaintiffs. As the six plaintiffs, including Li Haifeng, failed to reach an agreement on compensation with the three defendants, they filed this lawsuit.

Opinion of the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City:

Pursuant to Article 101 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law), citizens and legal persons enjoy the right to reputation, and the personal dignity of citizens is protected by law. The defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau has the statutory authority to investigate criminal cases. In the process of investigating the rape criminal case, it was not in violation of legal provisions to arrange for the six minor plaintiffs, including Li Haifeng, to assist in the mixed identification procedure and to take photographs and videos for investigative purposes. However, after the investigative activity of the mixed identification was completed, when providing relevant news materials to the defendant Anhui Television Station, the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, as a public security authority, should have realized and was obligated to particularly remind Anhui Television Station to perform relevant technical processing on the images when broadcasting, in order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the six plaintiffs. The Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau failed to fulfill this obligation. Anhui Television Station, as a news organization, should also have paid attention to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of others in its news reporting. However, when broadcasting the news in question, it performed some degree of technical processing on the facial images of the criminal suspect Zhu Moumou, but neglected to process the facial images of the six plaintiffs, causing their faces to be directly displayed on screen without any obscuration. Although the broadcast duration was short, it was sufficient for persons familiar with the six plaintiffs to recognize them from the television screen. Moreover, due to the wide coverage of television as a mass media platform, the news content spread widely in society, producing extensive effects. Additionally, when Anhui Television Station broadcast the news, it did not provide a special explanation regarding the six plaintiffs' assistance to the public security authority in the mixed identification, leading to misunderstandings among unspecified members of the public. As a result, the six plaintiffs were labeled as "rapists" by others, their social evaluations were severely lowered, and certain harmful consequences materialized. Both Anhui Television Station and the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau were subjectively at fault regarding the occurrence of these harmful consequences. Their acts infringed upon the reputation rights of the six plaintiffs, and they shall bear civil liability for compensation for the harmful consequences caused by their infringing acts. Pursuant to Article 120 of the General Principles of Civil Law, where a citizen's right to reputation is infringed, the infringer may be ordered to restore reputation, eliminate adverse effects, apologize, and compensate for losses. However, the scope of compensation for losses shall correspond to the scope of the adverse effects caused by the infringement. Both Anhui Television Station and the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau caused the infringement through negligence, without subjective intent to insult or defame others for personal gain. Therefore, the court does not support the six plaintiffs' request for RMB 600,000 in mental distress damages, and fixes the amount of mental distress damages at RMB 6,000 per person, totaling RMB 36,000.

The right to portraiture is the right of citizens to control their own likeness. Article 100 of the General Principles of Civil Law stipulates: Citizens enjoy the right to portraiture; the use of a citizen's likeness for profit-making purposes without the consent of the person concerned is not permitted. Therefore, infringement of the right to portraiture requires two elements: first, the use of a citizen's likeness without permission, and second, use for profit-making purposes. Neither the defendant Anhui Television Station nor the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau used the likenesses of Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs for profit-making purposes, and therefore, they did not infringe upon the portraiture rights of the six plaintiffs.

The defendant Yeji Experimental School, at the request of the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, assigned a teacher to lead Li Haifeng and the other five plaintiffs to the sub-bureau to assist in the detection of the relevant criminal case; this act was not improper. Regarding the acts of taking photos and videos during the identification process by the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, Yeji Experimental School had neither the power to interfere nor could it foresee that the image materials would be improperly disseminated by the news media. The defendant Anhui Television Station did not notify Yeji Experimental School before broadcasting the news in question. Therefore, the acts of Yeji Experimental School did not constitute infringement against the six plaintiffs.

In summary, the Baohe District People's Court of Hefei City rendered the following judgment on October 17, 2005:

1. The defendant Anhui Television Station and the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau shall publicly apologize to the plaintiffs Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, and Zhang Libao, so as to eliminate adverse effects and restore reputation (the content of the apology is subject to the court's approval). Should the two defendants fail to perform, the court shall publish the operative part of the final judgment in a provincial-level newspaper of Anhui Province, with the relevant costs borne jointly by Anhui Television Station and the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau.
2. The defendant Anhui Television Station and the defendant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau shall jointly pay each of the plaintiffs Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, and Zhang Libao RMB 6,000 in mental distress damages, totaling RMB 36,000.
3. The claims of the plaintiffs Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, and Zhang Libao against the defendant Yeji Experimental School are dismissed.
4. The other claims of the plaintiffs Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, and Zhang Libao are dismissed.

The Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, arguing:

1. In this case, the six appellees, including Li Haifeng, claimed that the original trial defendant Anhui Television Station and our bureau intentionally fabricated false news, infringing upon their portraiture and reputation rights. The first-instance court found that Anhui Television Station failed to fulfill its duty of care and our bureau failed to fulfill its duty of special reminder, thereby infringing upon the reputation rights of Li Haifeng and others. The nature of the legal relationship asserted by Li Haifeng and the other six persons is inconsistent with what the court found. The court should not have directly rendered the judgment but should have informed them to amend their claims, so that our bureau could present evidence on this point.
2. Our bureau provided news materials, including video recordings, as a result of a passive interview, fulfilling our duty of legal publicity. There was no subjective fault. Anhui Television Station came to the local area for interviews, filmed the school and the crime scene, and came to our bureau to obtain first-hand information on the case. In addition to comprehensively and objectively introducing the case, our bureau provided relevant video materials at the request of the reporter, not for the purpose of television broadcast, but for the reporter and editor to fully understand the case and ensure the accuracy of the news. If Anhui Television Station intended to broadcast the video materials provided by our bureau, it should have obtained our consent, but the television station failed to fulfill this obligation. The first-instance court's holding that our bureau had a duty of special reminder and that we should bear tort liability has no factual or legal basis.
3. When Anhui Television Station broadcast the news in question, it had already performed technical processing. The first-instance court's finding that the appellees' faces were directly displayed on the screen without any obscuration, and that this constituted a failure to protect their legitimate rights and interests, is erroneous. Our bureau believes that although it was improper for the television station to edit and broadcast the video without notifying our bureau and obtaining our consent, the content broadcast allowed the audience to clearly distinguish that Li Haifeng and the other five appellees were not the criminal suspects. The purpose of the broadcast was to promote justice, expose crime, and publicize the law, which has the effect of defeating wrongfulness. In summary, our bureau's acts did not constitute infringement and should not bear civil liability. We request that the second-instance court amend the judgment.

Appellees' Response (Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, Zhang Libao): The facts found in the first-instance judgment are clear, and the conclusion is correct. The appellant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, when providing the relevant video materials to the original trial defendant Anhui Television Station, should have fulfilled its duty of special reminder. It was precisely because Anhui Television Station did not perform technical processing on the appellees' facial images when broadcasting the video materials that the appellees' reputation was damaged. Therefore, the grounds of appeal of the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau are untenable, and we request that the second-instance court uphold the original judgment.

Original Trial Defendant Anhui Television Station's Statement: The appellant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau's ground of appeal that our station's broadcast of the video materials in question required the sub-bureau's consent is unsound. The amount of mental distress damages awarded to Li Haifeng and the other five appellees in the original judgment is unreasonable.

Original Trial Defendant Yeji Experimental School's Statement: The public security department lawfully arranged for the students to participate in the identification. Our school's cooperation with the public security authority was not improper. The original trial defendant Anhui Television Station broadcast the identification process without prior notice to our school, so our school was not at fault. The first-instance judgment that our school bears no liability is correct.

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance after trial.

Issues in Dispute:

1. Whether the nature of the legal relationship asserted in the first-instance claims of the appellees, including Li Haifeng, was consistent with the determination of the first-instance court.
2. Whether the public security authority was at fault for failing to fulfill a duty of special reminder when providing video materials formed during the investigation to the news media. Whether the legality of the public security authority's investigative acts, the legitimacy of cooperating with news media for legal publicity, and the negligence of the news media itself in news reporting constitute statutory grounds for exempting the public security authority from the aforesaid fault.

Opinion of the Hefei Intermediate People's Court:

The first-instance claims of the appellees Li Haifeng, Gao Ping, Liu Lei, Sun Jun, Chen Guanggui, and Zhang Libao were that the appellant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau and the original trial defendants Anhui Television Station and Yeji Experimental School had infringed their reputation and portraiture rights, and they requested that the three entities publicly apologize, restore reputation, eliminate adverse effects, and pay mental distress damages of RMB 600,000. The first-instance court tried the case based on these claims, found that Anhui Television Station and the Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau had failed to fulfill their respective obligations, thereby infringing the reputation rights of the appellees, but that their acts did not infringe the portraiture rights of the appellees, and rendered a corresponding judgment. This judgment did not exceed the scope of the claims raised by the appellees in the first instance. Therefore, the appellant's argument that the legal relationship determined in the first-instance judgment was inconsistent with the appellees' first-instance claims is untenable.

Pursuant to Article 3 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the public security organs are responsible for the investigation, detention, execution of arrest, and preliminary inquiry of criminal cases. In order to better combat crime, public security organs may, when exercising their investigative powers, adopt certain special investigative measures in accordance with the law as needed for their work. In this case, the appellant, Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, arranged for the six appellees, including Li Haifeng, to participate in a mixed identification procedure to assist in solving the relevant criminal cases, which is a statutory and special investigative measure. The conduct of Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau in conducting the mixed identification in a specific, non-public venue for the purpose of case investigation, and in recording and archiving the process, was an exercise of its investigative powers in accordance with the law and was not in itself unlawful. However, after the conclusion of the investigative activities, when providing materials generated during the investigation to the news media, the public security organ should exercise a duty of care to avoid infringing upon the lawful rights of others. If, due to failure to exercise such duty of care, the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations are infringed upon, corresponding legal liability shall be incurred. The provision of news materials by a public security organ to the news media is not an exercise of investigative powers in accordance with the law, and the legitimacy of the exercise of investigative powers itself does not exempt the organ from legal liability for failing to exercise due care when providing materials to the news media. According to the facts of this case, Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau provided the mixed identification video recording to the original trial defendant, Anhui TV Station, after the conclusion of the mixed identification investigative measure. Moreover, Anhui TV Station is a news media organization; it collected the investigative materials solely for news reporting purposes. The provision of materials generated during the investigation by Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau to Anhui TV Station was not a continuation of the investigative measure. Therefore, the legality of the investigative conduct of Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau does not constitute a statutory ground for exemption from liability for its failure to exercise due care when providing materials related to the solved case to the news media.

The appellant, Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau, argued that it was not at fault, claiming that it was merely cooperating with news work and fulfilling its obligation of legal propaganda. This reflects a misunderstanding of the legal concept of "fault." Fault in civil law includes both intent and negligence. The fact that an actor has good intentions does not necessarily mean that he is free from fault. The purpose of broadcasting legal programs, as Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau stated, is to promote justice and expose crime, serving the needs of legal propaganda. However, in this case, the promotion of legal awareness and the protection of the lawful rights and interests of minors are not contradictory. For special cases involving minors, when producing news programs intended for a broad, unspecified audience, applying technical processing to the images of minors or providing special explanations in the program would not affect the effectiveness of promoting legal awareness and justice. The police officers involved in the identification knew and understood the content of the mixed identification and would not assume that a person unrelated to the case was a criminal suspect merely because that person participated in the identification; thus, the social evaluation of these innocent persons would not be lowered. However, when Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau handed over the mixed identification video recording to the television station, it failed to exercise a special duty to remind, resulting in the facial images of the six appellees, including Li Haifeng, being broadcast to an unspecified audience through the news without any technical processing, and the news program also made no special explanation in this regard. Ordinary viewers of the news may not necessarily know the specific content of the mixed identification, a particular investigative measure. Therefore, some people publicly accused the six appellees of committing heinous crimes at a young age, labeling them as "rapists," leading to a decrease in their social evaluation and resulting in damage to their right to reputation. Consequently, the legitimacy of Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau's cooperation with the news media for legal propaganda does not constitute a statutory ground for exempting it from the civil liability it should bear in this case.

The occurrence of the damage in this case is also related to the negligence of the original trial defendant, Anhui TV Station. If Anhui TV Station had applied some technical processing during the broadcast, the damage would not have occurred, given that Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau failed to fulfill its duty to remind. However, the negligence of the news media itself in news reporting does not relieve Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau of its liability. Pursuant to Article 7, Item (2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over the Right to Reputation, if news materials are provided passively, but the provider consents to or acquiesces in the publication, resulting in damage to another person's reputation, the provider's conduct shall be deemed to constitute infringement of the right to reputation. A television station is a news media organization facing the general public. When Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau was interviewed by Anhui TV Station's "First Time" program and provided the mixed identification video recording to the station without any special explanation, this constituted an implied consent to the station's broadcast of the material. The negligence of Anhui TV Station itself in news reporting does not constitute a statutory ground for exempting Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau from civil liability.

In summary, the appellant Yeji Public Security Sub-bureau's grounds of appeal that it should not bear civil tort liability are all untenable. The facts found in the first instance were clear, and the judgment was correct. However, in the application of law, Article 7, Item (2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over the Right to Reputation should also have been applied, and this should be supplemented. Accordingly, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on March 15, 2006:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment affirmed.

Note: All names of parties involved in this case are pseudonyms.
